purpose: Docker Engine remote API, used to manage containers, images, networks, and volumes on the host.
description: The Docker Engine API allows full control over the container runtime — creating, starting, and inspecting containers. When exposed over TCP without TLS client authentication (the default on port 2375, versus the TLS-only 2376), anyone who can reach the port has unauthenticated root-equivalent control of the host.
misconfigurations: Docker socket exposed via a reverse proxy without auth
TLS enabled but client certificate verification skipped
attack_patterns: Mount the host filesystem into a new privileged container for full read/write host access
Deploy a container that reads host secrets or SSH keys
Use the API to pull and run cryptomining images at scale
real_world_incidents: Mass-scanning campaigns (e.g. the 2019-2020 Docker API worm activity) routinely find and exploit open 2375/2376 ports within minutes of exposure, deploying cryptominers.
recommended_actions: Never bind the Docker daemon to a TCP port reachable from outside localhost without mutual TLS.
If remote access is required, enable TLS with client certificate verification (dockerd --tlsverify).
Prefer the Unix socket plus SSH tunneling over exposing the API on the network at all.
Restrict access with a firewall/security group even when TLS is enabled, as defense in depth.

audience_guidance.student: Docker's API is like a remote control for creating and running programs in isolated boxes (containers). If that remote control is left unlocked on the network, anyone can use it to run their own programs — including ones that break out of the box and take over the whole computer.
audience_guidance.developer: Never start dockerd with -H tcp://0.0.0.0:2375. If you need remote Docker access, use --tlsverify with client certificates, or tunnel over SSH instead of exposing the API directly.
audience_guidance.bug_bounty_hunter: An open 2375 is often an instant critical: `docker -H tcp://target:2375 info` confirms access, then a privileged container with the host filesystem mounted gives full host compromise.
audience_guidance.pentester: Confirm unauthenticated access, then run a container with `-v /:/host --privileged` to chroot into the host filesystem and demonstrate full compromise.
audience_guidance.security_team: Treat any host with 2375 reachable from outside localhost as a critical incident — it is equivalent to an exposed root shell. Audit all Docker hosts for TLS enforcement.
